Governance review

If 4853 passes

A temporary supervisor would investigate the A272 dispute. The proposal seeks removal-facilitation powers, but does not itself remove Vini or change the board’s signing threshold.

What 4853 proposes

Proposal 4853 asks Terra governance to appoint the named emergency supervisor, Martin, to investigate the dispute surrounding A272. It also expressly asks for the removal-facilitation powers in bylaw Article 2.4.5.4. Those powers, and the limits on them, matter as much as the investigation.

What happens if 4853 passes?

Scroll sideways to read all columns.

StepEffect
AppointmentThe nominee must accept in writing and declare independence. The bylaws require acceptance within 30 days; otherwise the appointment is deemed rejected.
InvestigationThe supervisor is instructed to hear all four directors, review relevant records and decide remedies for the A272 dispute.
Possible removalItem 4 expressly invokes Article 2.4.5.4: instructions to facilitate a member’s removal where considered necessary or desirable to resolve the adverse event. It names no director for automatic removal.
Duration and costUp to four weeks from written acceptance; an extension needs explicit Terra governance approval. Compensation is capped at USD 10,000.
On-chain changesThe proposal contains no executable messages. It does not itself remove a member, change the 75% threshold, transfer contract roles or cancel grants. Any such change needs a further implementation step.

The bylaws contain an important tension. Article 2.4.5.4 provides a route for removal instructions, while Article 2.6.2 limits the supervisor to investigation and remedies and restricts direct removal, replacement and direction of board decisions. The proposal invokes the former and remains subject to the latter. A written explanation of the permitted process is needed before treating either unrestricted removal power or a purely advisory role as settled.

Article 1.10 also allows the binding effect of the veto body to be disregarded during an emergency appointment. That is a weakening of a governance safeguard under the bylaws; it does not automatically disable a veto contract. Terra governance can remove the emergency supervisor under Article 2.6.4.

A272 failed. Could 4853 achieve the same removal?

It could reopen a route to that outcome. On 3 October, 0xphilipp proposed A272 to remove Vini and convert the board to two-of-three approval. It failed: 0xphilipp and MB voted YES, Rose voted NO and Vini cast no ballot. On 24 October, the same proposer submitted 4853, defining the emergency around the unresolved A272 dispute and expressly seeking removal-facilitation powers.

The public discussion makes the concern concrete. In post 57, 0xphilipp argued for separating removal from replacement and discussed a temporary two-of-three board. The final 4853 text does not guarantee that replacements join before a removal, maintain a minimum board size, or prevent two remaining directors from becoming sufficient approval authority.

This is an alternative process following a failed removal proposal. It is reasonable to scrutinize whether it could produce the same membership change without preserving the previous checks. The evidence does not establish that the supervisor will remove Vini or that the outcome has been agreed in advance.

The proposer’s response

4853 requires an independent, impartial review, hearing all four directors and examining any director’s conduct where relevant. In post 55, 0xphilipp denied a voting agreement with MB and said a five-member, three-of-five board could be recommended. In post 57, 0xphilipp offered an off-chain commitment to vote only NO or ABSTAIN during a temporary two-of-three period, except when onboarding new independent directors.

That offer is material, but it is not an on-chain restriction or a condition written into 4853. A signed agreement and its enforcement have not been verified. In post 97, Vini withdrew support for the named candidate, citing an allegedly undisclosed ERIS relationship. The withdrawal is a public first-party statement; the alleged relationship has not been independently verified.

Would removing Vini leave grant interests in control?

Removing Vini would remove a director who opposed the earlier Estima grant. It would leave 0xphilipp’s ERIS/Creda grant relationship and MB’s Superbolt representative relationship in place. Removal alone would not resolve those interests, require their recusal from future payments, or complete the contract handover.

Vini was not the only recorded dissenting director. Rose also rejected Estima A258 and cast the only NO on A272. Vini has a separate 16,900-USDC audit-payment interest. Independent review should apply the same disclosure, recusal and acceptance standards to all four directors.

These are conditional calculations for the Stewardship multisig, assuming equal seat weights. Board meetings and contract execution have different rules; Article 3.1.3.2(c) retains the signing threshold for actions requiring the multisig. Any later membership or threshold change must be assessed from its actual executable messages.

Safeguards holders should ask for

  • Publish findings and let each affected director respond before a removal is implemented.
  • Review all four directors’ relevant grants, payment approvals and retained powers under the same written scope.
  • Require an approved replacement and threshold arrangement that prevents two interested directors from becoming sufficient approval authority.
  • Publish the supervisor’s independence declaration, any voting commitment, the treatment of the veto body and the exact removal or upgrade process.
  • Creda’s 210,000-USDC grant and milestone approvals
  • Vini and MB: payments, project relationships and dissent
  • Recorded director votes and their coverage
  • Bylaws and signing-threshold requirement

Three voting systems

Native accounts and validators

A delegator ballot overrides its validator’s option for that delegation. It does not erase the validator’s ballot or transfer ownership of the validator.

The ampLUNA hub

The hub holds native LUNA delegations. Its authorized vote operator can cast a normal or weighted native ballot. This affects native delegator power only—not Phoenix/TLA synthetic Alliance weight.

The vAMP prop-gauge

Vote-escrow holders accumulate proposal-specific voting power. After a 10% participation quorum, the gauge can ask the hub to cast a weighted or currently wanted vote. The large account can meet this quorum alone, but had not voted in the captured gauge records.

Lion DAO voted before its internal vote closed

  1. 24 Oct · 15:28 UTC

    RyanLion voted YES on A33

    The ballot carried 60.002B ROAR: 26.154% of total eligible power and 99.866% of YES power.

  2. 25 Oct · 05:06 UTC

    Lion DAO’s validator changed ABSTAIN to YES

    The DAO’s A33 vote was still open when its validator changed to YES.

  3. 26 Oct · 13:16 UTC

    A33’s voting window ended

    The final DAO ratio was 30.43% YES, 1.875% NO and 67.70% ABSTAIN. Both the DAO and validator ultimately favoured YES.

Attribution confidence: high for the transaction, ballot and voting-power facts; moderate for the DAO-interface display name “RyanLion,” pending a first-party profile declaration. No real-world identity is inferred.

A Think Tank wallet transferred 513,657.706575846 ROAR to the RyanLion wallet on 22 October. The transfer and profile link support an operational relationship, not sole identity, ownership or motive. The transfer does not explain the much larger voting position.

What remains unresolved

Obtain the final tally and complete gauge history; entity-level interest disclosures; hosting and payment agreements; validator-mandate rules; historical Think Tank membership and notification records; and an explanation for the empty P5 veto message. Current evidence does not prove vote buying, a unified ERIS bloc, or ERIS control of the large vAMP account.
